That’s the wrong period/basis: the relevant comparator is FY2025Q3→FY2026Q3 (or at least the immediate FY2024Q3→FY2025Q3 trend, which Deere reported as −9% YoY to $12,018m). Using a boom-year 2022→2023 growth rate to project 2026 mechanically overstates “Worldwide net sales and revenues.”
Diluted EPS (GAAP): critic raised a concrete objection: Wrong basis: The model says “post‑guidance signal: none found,” but Deere routinely provides and updates full‑year guidance, and by Q2 FY2026 (May 2026) it had issued FY2026 net income guidance in its earnings release/8‑K. Projecting FY2026Q3 GAAP diluted EPS by applying a median of historical YoY EPS changes to FY2025Q3 (4.75) without reconciling to that FY2026 full‑year guidance is an invalid basis and likely yields a quarterly EPS inconsistent with the company’s guided full‑year outcome. This can be checked directly against Deere’s Q2 FY2026 earnings materials.
Production & Precision Ag operating prof: critic raised a concrete objection: Over-precision: Deere reports segment operating profit to the nearest $1 million, and your anchor ($580m) and growth rates are themselves rounded. At minimum this should be rounded to USDm with no decimals (≈$378m), otherwise the figure is misleading on a unit/basis level.
